suggestions.after:
# Hello World!

## Getting Started

Follow these steps to set up your Hello-World project:

### 1. Create a project directory
```bash
$ mkdir ~/Hello-World
```
This creates a directory for your project called "Hello-World" in your home directory.

### 2. Navigate to the directory
```bash
$ cd ~/Hello-World
```
This changes the current working directory to your newly created directory.

### 3. Initialize a Git repository
```bash
$ git init
```
This sets up the necessary Git files. You should see output like:
```
Initialized empty Git repository in /Users/your_user_directory/Hello-World/.git/
```

### 4. Create a README file
```bash
$ touch README
```
On Windows, use: `type nul > README`

recommendations.description: Restructure the README with proper markdown formatting. Commands and descriptions are currently concatenated without separation, making them difficult to read and copy-paste. Use code blocks and clear visual hierarchy.

Improve explanation of shell conventions. Terms like tilde (~) and placeholder paths (/Users/your_user_directory/) should be clearly explained for users unfamiliar with command-line interfaces.
